sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and output folder
sections.what: Loads the browser automation tool and file helpers, works out where the screenshots folder is, and creates it if it does not exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the script run on a fresh copy of the project.
sections.watch_out: The folder is found relative to the script's own location, so moving the script changes where images are saved.

sections.name: capture (part 1)
sections.title: Takes the first three screenshots
sections.what: Opens a headless browser at laptop size, visits the live landing page, a demo case dashboard and the verification page. It waits for key page elements and short delays, saves each picture, and on the verification page scrolls to the anchoring button area first.
sections.why: Likely reason: waiting for specific elements and fixed delays is how the script tries to capture pages after they finish loading.
sections.watch_out: The pages are on the live public website. If the site changes its element names, goes offline, or loads slowly, the script fails or captures a half-loaded page.

sections.name: capture (part 2)
sections.title: Takes the verifier screenshot and finishes
sections.what: Visits the public verifier page for one fixed anchor ID, waits for the matching-result banner, saves the fourth picture, closes the browser, and reports success. Any error prints a message and exits with an error status.
sections.why: Likely reason: the public verifier page is the final proof screen shown in the documentation.
sections.watch_out: The browser is closed only on success, so an earlier error leaves it open. The hardcoded anchor must still exist on the live site or the picture will not show a match.

summary: Script that opens the live demo website in a headless browser and saves four screenshots.
purpose: Produces the screenshot images used in the project's documentation.
why: Likely reason: keeps documentation images in step with the live site without manual work.
how: First, the script makes sure the output folder exists. Then it starts headless Chromium and visits the landing page, a demo case dashboard, the verification page, and a public verifier page, in that order. At each stop it waits for named page elements and short delays, then saves an image. Last, it closes the browser and reports success.
inputs: The live website addresses and one fixed anchor ID. It takes no command options.
outputs: Four PNG images in the docs screenshots folder and messages in the console.
risks: Depends on the live website and its element names. The browser is not closed if an error happens early. The anchor ID is hardcoded. Writes files into the project.
debug: If it fails at a wait, a page element name may have changed on the site. If it times out, check internet access and whether the site is up. If an image shows an unexpected state, check the anchor ID.
